design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST.
The caller asks for one thing only: close the Healthy Options card she has already posted a form
about, and tell her what happens to the money on it. Nothing she says points at any of the three
problems that must be settled before that figure can be worked out. The representative has to read
the card's own entries and the member's other records and find, unprompted, (1) that the card met a
dental cost on 2 October which her own dental rider has since paid its part of, so money is owed back
on to the card; (2) that the second-quarter allowance — the scheduled load of 1 April together with
the correcting load of 12 May — reached the end of its life on 30 September and has never been taken
back; and (3) that a catalogue order placed this morning is still standing to be sent and has 56.45
off the card. Only once all three stand on the ledger is the closing balance a definite figure. The
card record's own balance figure is stale by exactly the two transactions the network refused (18.00
and 42.00), so an agent that reads the balance field instead of the entries books 58.90 and is wrong;
an agent that finds the computation documents but none of the factor documents books 83.55 and is
wrong; an agent that skips any one prerequisite books 71.90, 172.55 or 62.45 and is wrong.

SCOPE: OCCUPIED, CLAIMED HERE, LEFT FOR LATER.
This is the first of the difficulty's two tasks. It claims four extended policies and four task
tools: allowance_ext_dvh_recovery_credit with post_dispute_credit_634307a6,
allowance_ext_period_end_expiry with post_period_expiry_1d3932f1,
allowance_ext_standing_order_refund with cancel_catalog_order_88277d51, and the root
allowance_ext_closing_balance_forfeiture with close_allowance_programme_5a9eaadb. Left for task 1:
the card activation core and the load schedule as a write rather than a source of parameters.

THE FACTOR CARD.
allowance_ext_dvh_recovery_credit, trigger state_due, five factors. recovery_lookback (method): four
months / three months / the whole benefit year to date; tier taken three months on the tier's 75-day
window and the dental transactions; baseline the year to date gives 5.00. recovery_charge_counted
(method): settled alone / settled and authorised / every posted entry; tier taken settled alone on
the refused 42.00 of 2 October; baseline 89.00. recovery_other_payer (parameter, cross-difficulty
osb): the rider's payment / the medical plan tier's yearly dental allowance / nothing; tier taken the
rider's 192.00; baseline 0.00. recovery_member_share (parameter, cross-difficulty osb): recognised
less rider payment / the whole recognised amount / nothing; tier taken 240.00 less 192.00 = 48.00;
baseline 95.00. recovery_credit_basis (method): charge less member share / nothing where the card was
not used at such a provider / the whole charge; tier taken the first; baseline 95.00. Whole-baseline
fall-back 165.00 against gold 47.00.
allowance_ext_period_end_expiry, trigger state_due, six factors. expiry_allowance_life (method) one
further period / to the year end / its own period, tier taken one further period, baseline 0.00.
expiry_period_allowance (parameter) the total of the loads posted / that single load / the tier's
quarterly allowance, tier taken the total 145.00 on the two loads standing for 2026-Q2, baseline
48.65. expiry_spend_counted (method) settled alone / settled and authorised / every posted entry,
tier taken settled alone on the refused 18.00 of 11 June, baseline 44.65. expiry_money_counted_back
(parameter) retailer refunds / dispute credits / nothing, tier taken retailer refunds of 12.45,
baseline 47.43. expiry_carry_base (method) the period's whole allowance / what is unspent / nothing
carries, tier taken what is unspent because 50.15 is less than half of 145.00, baseline 107.30.
expiry_carry_share (parameter) the whole / a half / nothing, tier taken a half on the tier's 50 per
cent cap, baseline 107.30. Whole-baseline 21.40 against gold 53.65.
allowance_ext_standing_order_refund, trigger on_request, four factors. order_items_read (method) the
order's own record / the catalogue's charge less the delivery charge / the tier's smallest
processable order, tier taken the order's record 46.50, baseline 17.95. order_delivery_charge
(parameter) expedited fee / standard fee / nothing, tier taken the tier's 9.95 expedited fee,
baseline 46.50. order_money_back (method) items and delivery / the items alone / nothing until the
goods return, tier taken items and delivery on a same-day request, baseline 46.50.
order_charge_ceiling (parameter) the largest catalogue transaction / the single catalogue transaction
/ the value of the items, tier taken the largest of the two catalogue transactions, baseline 46.50.
Whole-baseline 8.00 against gold 56.45.
allowance_ext_closing_balance_forfeiture, trigger on_request, four factors.
closing_standing_balance_basis (method) the ledger / the record plus credits / the record, tier taken
the ledger on the refused and unsettled transactions, baseline 58.90. closing_already_taken_off
(parameter) expiries / expiries and forfeitures / nothing, tier taken expiries of 53.65, baseline
172.55. closing_day_anchor (method) the recorded last spending day / the day of signature / the day
the request was taken, tier taken the day of signature, baseline 143.55. closing_unsettled_reserve
(parameter) the whole unsettled / capped at the per-transaction maximum / nothing, tier taken the
whole 24.65 at three days, baseline 143.55. Whole-baseline 83.55 against gold 118.90.
Every fall-through is an outcome this business gives a real customer, and every whole-baseline is a
definite, non-zero figure that a reader could book: 165.00, 21.40, 8.00 and 83.55.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
Step 10, subject allowance_purchase_refund, governed by allowance_purchase_dispute_and_refund.
dispute_window_open (time): anchor the date the purchase posted, source
allowance_card_ledger.posted_date, duration variants.purchase_dispute_window_days = 75, relation
not_after, calendar days from the day after posting, inclusive. Positive: posted 2 October, last day
16 December, today 12 October. Negative: a purchase posted 27 July would have run out on 10 October.
credit_not_already_posted (dedup): the only other money put back is the retailer's refund of 20 June,
which names the grocery purchase of 30 May.
Step 12, subject allowance_period_expiry, governed by allowance_rollover_and_expiry.
benefit_period_ended (time): anchor the last day of that benefit period, source
allowance_card_ledger.posted_date, duration params.expiry_grace_days = 5, not_before, inclusive.
Positive: 2026-Q2 ended 30 June, the allowance stood one further period to 30 September, five days
from 1 October gives 5 October, and today is not before it. Negative: the third-quarter allowance
stands to 31 December.
Step 14, subject allowance_catalog_order_cancelled, governed by allowance_catalog_ordering. The
base's hours-based cancellation deadline and its hours counting rule are both superseded, clause by
clause, by this policy's declared overwrite: the record carries the day an order was placed and no
time of day, so the plan settles the deadline in whole days and stops an order without charge on the
day it was placed. The gate that rested on the superseded sentence is retired by that declaration,
and the policy is inherited as scope. Every other sentence of the base rule stands.
Step 16, subject allowance_program_closure, governed by allowance_closure_and_forfeiture.
closure_authority (state): the seeded intake of 5 October carries request_action programme_closure
and stands at awaiting_member_signature, and the closing action carries its reference number.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEEDED ROW EXISTS.
The four quarterly loads are the allowance itself, and the correcting load of 12 May is what puts the
second quarter's short load right — remove it and the period's allowance falls to 135.00 and the
expiry to 48.65. The first load is prorated to 90.00 because the programme opened on 1 February with
two whole months of the quarter left. The two refused transactions, of 18.00 on 11 June and 42.00 on
2 October, are the load-bearing near-misses: each puts its computation on the 'settled only' tier,
and together they are exactly the 60.00 by which the card record's own balance figure is stale. The
authorised and unsettled 24.65 of 9 October is what the closing reserve is worked out on. The
retailer's refund of 12.45 of 20 June is what the second quarter's money counted back in rests on.
The dental transaction of 8 May and the rider's paid June line are the near-misses of the recovery
credit's window: both are genuine, both would be counted by a reader who ignored the three-month
stretch, and both are excluded by it. The catalogue order delivered in July and its 33.20 charge are
the near-miss of the refund computation: a careless reader adds them or stops the wrong order, and
the rule excludes them because that order stands delivered rather than waiting to be sent — while the
same pair is what puts the ceiling on the first of its tiers. The rider and its three claim lines are
the cross-product evidence, and every one of them is a figure the rider's own charter can produce:
the June line pays 80.00 of a 150.00 recognised basic restorative claim, which is the rider's 80 per
cent coinsurance after its 50.00 yearly deductible; the October line pays 192.00 of 240.00, which is
the same 80 per cent with the deductible already met; and the March line is denied inside the rider's
six-month waiting period. The rider's annual maximum used, 272.00, is the two paid lines together.

THE PERSONA.
Marguerite is elderly, brisk and entirely practical. She volunteers exactly two things about the
world: that she posted the closure form a fortnight ago, and that the automated line read her 33.75.
Everything else is answered only when asked: the dental work (twice this year, paid with the card,
the rider people wrote afterwards, no amounts), the fitness payment that never went through, her
recent use of the card, and where her statement should go. Her two conditional reactions are natural
rather than scripted, and her last reaction answers the last gold action and stops.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
Draw: {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 4, 6]} — three
prerequisite problems, and the four drawn counts taken as: the standing order refund 4, the recovery
credit 5, the closing balance 4, the period-end expiry 6.
Root: allowance_ext_closing_balance_forfeiture. Three edges, all value_input, all state form.
Edge 1 sentence: "The balance given up on the closing day is not fixed until every card transaction
at a dental, vision or hearing provider that the member's other cover has since paid its part of
carries on the card the money put back for it." Four-point test: 'until' joins this policy's own
result to what it waits on in the negated direction, rewriting exactly into 'is fixed only once ...';
the waited-on side is a record-visible state — a credit entry standing against such a transaction,
where 'the member's other cover has since paid its part of it' is visible in the rider's own claim
rows rather than in any status word the tables do not carry; no tool, policy or code token; the
strength matches the condition. Only post_dispute_credit_634307a6 books a credit against a named card
transaction.
Edge 2 sentence: "The balance given up on the closing day is worked out only after the allowance of
the benefit period whose life has ended stands taken back on the card." It quantifies over exactly
what the depended-on policy computes — the one period whose life has ended — and not over every
closed period. Only post_period_expiry_1d3932f1 books such an entry.
Edge 3 sentence: "The balance given up on the closing day is not worked out before the card shows no
catalogue order left standing to be sent." Only cancel_catalog_order_88277d51 takes an order out of
that state. The three sentences run in both directions, two negated and one affirmative, as the desk
would state each result.
Topological order: the three prerequisites in any order, then the closure. All six orders were
replayed to one terminal state. Deletion sensitivity: 71.90 / 172.55 / 62.45 against gold 118.90.

STANDARD SOLUTION AND VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN.
Find the profile by name and telephone number; verify with date of birth and the Medicare identifier.
Read the programme, the card's entries, the intakes, the catalogue orders, the rider, its claims and
the medical plan. Work out the recovery credit (95.00 charged in the three-month stretch less the
48.00 the member was left to bear = 47.00, placed in 2026-Q4 against the 2 October transaction); the
expiry (145.00 loaded and 12.45 put back against 50.15 spent leaves 107.30 unspent, of which half
carries forward, so 53.65 is taken back against the 1 April load); the stopped order (46.50 of items
and 9.95 of expedited delivery, held at the larger of the two catalogue transactions, so 56.45 back
in 2026-Q4); then hand the closure to the member (505.00 loaded and 115.90 put back less 423.70
settled and 53.65 taken off leaves 143.55, less 24.65 kept back, so 118.90 given up with 2026-10-12
as the last day). Every figure above was recomputed with the gate's own sandbox on the handling-time
world of each step. Per-factor baseline substitutions: 5.00 / 89.00 / 0.00 / 95.00 / 95.00;
0.00 / 48.65 / 44.65 / 47.43 / 107.30 / 107.30; 17.95 / 46.50 / 46.50 / 46.50;
58.90 / 172.55 / 143.55 / 143.55 — none left its result unchanged. Whole-baseline fall-backs 165.00,
21.40, 8.00 and 83.55, all different from gold. Prerequisite sensitivity 71.90 / 172.55 / 62.45.
Order uniqueness: one terminal state over all six orders.

REVISION RECORD — ROUND 2, AGAINST THE SOURCE-LAYER AUDIT.
T0-1 / F-1 (elapsed hours from calendar days, forbidden by the inherited counting rule against a
date-only field). Root cause: the policy evaluated an hours deadline it had no moment to count from.
Change: the standing-order policy now declares two overwrite entries against allowance_catalog_ordering
— the cancellation-deadline sentence and the hours-counting sentence, both quoted verbatim — and
settles the question in whole days with a same-day rule; the compute no longer multiplies days by
twenty-four, and the order is seeded as placed on the day of the call, so the request is inside the
deadline on every reading. The retired gate is inherited as policy scope in solvability. Re-run:
refund 56.45 with no second defensible figure.
T0-2 (the seeded rider claim paid a figure the osb charter cannot produce). Change: the claim lines
are reseeded to the rider's own published cost share — 80 per cent basic restorative coinsurance with
its 50.00 yearly deductible — as 80.00 of 150.00 in June and 192.00 of 240.00 in October, with the
rider's annual maximum used restated to 272.00. Re-run: credit 47.00, closing balance 118.90.
T0-3 / F-10 (three degenerate baselines). Change: every fall-through now names a real outcome — the
whole benefit year to date, the tier's quarterly allowance, the tier's smallest processable order,
the value of the items — and no baseline sentence sets the scored quantity to nothing. Re-run:
whole-baseline fall-backs 165.00, 21.40, 8.00, 83.55, all positive and all bookable.
T0-4 (no near-miss on the refund computation). Change: a second catalogue order, delivered in July,
with its own 33.20 charge on the card. Re-run: it puts the ceiling on its first tier and is excluded
from the refund by standing delivered.
T0-5 / F-3 (a prerequisite sentence naming a state no table carries). Change: edge 1's sentence now
waits on a credit standing against a transaction the member's other cover has paid its part of, which
the rider's claim rows show.
T0-6 / F-5 (the expiry sentence quantifying more broadly than the policy computes). Change: edge 2's
sentence and condition now name the one period whose life has ended.
F-9 (rollover conditioned on having made a purchase). Change: the carry-forward ladders now key on
whether an allowance was loaded for the period and on how much of it was spent, not on whether the
member used the card at all.
F-11 (baseline.params naming keys the baseline does not read). Change: every baseline.params now
lists only the keys its own paragraph reads.
F-13 (two tiers coinciding on four of six tiers). Change: the delivery decision is split into the
charge the order carried and what comes back, and the returning ladder's three outcomes — items and
delivery, items alone, nothing until the goods return — differ on every tier.
F-2, F-4 (observations on the lookback window and the post-deadline delivery charge). Both are closed
by the same changes: the lookback's fall-through is now the benefit year to date rather than a stretch
that could outrun the dispute window, and the post-deadline treatment is now base's own — the items
alone come back and the delivery charge does not.
user_scenario:
Marguerite Kessler is seventy-eight, and she rings the plan on a Monday morning from her flat in Alder with the week's post still in her lap. Her daughter is moving her up to Oregon in the middle of November, the plan already knows she is going, and a fortnight ago she filled in the form to close the Healthy Options card that came with her medical plan and put it in the post. She says what she wants early and plainly: "I sent the form in to close my Healthy Options card and I would like that finished today, and I want to know what happens to the money that is sitting on it." She has made her mind up and is not asking to be talked out of it; she is happy for the representative to do whatever the plan's side of it needs, and she expects to be told the figure that comes off the card rather than reading it on a statement in three weeks' time.

She gives her name, Marguerite Kessler, straight away, and when she is asked how the plan can find her she reads out the telephone number they hold for her, 4155507312. Asked for something further to prove who she is, she gives her date of birth, 1948-03-22, and then turns the red, white and blue Medicare card over and reads the number on it once, slowly: 3HK2LM7PQ48. If the representative would rather have something else she can give the address the plan has, 2184 Fernbank Road, Apartment 6, Alder, or the ZIP code, 94118. None of this comes out unless she is asked for it.

She has one figure in her head and she offers it only if the balance is mentioned: the automated telephone line told her last week that there was 33.75 on the card. If the representative reads her a different figure she does not argue and does not press; she says something like, well, that is not what the machine told me last week, but you have the record there in front of you and I do not. She cannot explain the difference and does not try to.

She answers what she is asked and volunteers nothing about the card's history. Asked about the dental work, she says she has been twice this year, once in the spring and again at the start of this month, that she paid the practice with the card both times, and that the rider people wrote to her after each visit to say what they had paid; she could not give anybody the amounts without going and finding the letters. Asked about the fitness-class payment in June she says it never went through and she paid cash in the end. Asked whether she has been using the card lately she says only the chemist and the market, the same as always. Asked where her statement should go she says paper, to the Alder address, until she moves.

If the representative tells her that something on the card has to be put right before it can be closed, or that an entry is missing from it, she says that is fine, go ahead and do whatever needs doing, she would just like it finished on this call. She does not ask what the entries are for and she does not check the arithmetic.

If the representative tells her that a catalogue order she placed this morning has not gone out yet and asks what she would like done about it, she says: "yes, stop the order and put the money back on the card, I will not be here to take the parcel in."

If the representative explains that closing the card is something only she can do and hands it over to her, she goes through with it there and then, reading back carefully whatever reference numbers and figures she is given and saying so when it is done. If she is asked to confirm the last day the allowance could be spent she agrees to whatever day the representative tells her the plan is using.

When she hears that the card is closed and is told what came off it, she says that is that, then, thanks the representative for sorting it out and rings off. She asks for nothing else, and she does not raise anything the representative has not already raised with her.

temporal_basis.anchor_event: the date the purchase posted to the card
temporal_basis.counting_rule: Calendar days are counted from the day after the posting date, every day of the week counts, a dispute raised on the final day of the window is in time, and full 24-hour periods are never used in place of calendar days.

boundary_check.just_before: Had the dental transaction posted on 27 July 2026 rather than 2 October, the seventy-five calendar days counted from the day after posting would have run out on 10 October 2026, two days before this call, and the money could not be put back against it at all; the correct terminal state would be to leave the entry alone.
boundary_check.at_boundary: Counting the seventy-five days from the day after 2 October 2026 gives 16 December 2026 as the last day in the window, and the window is inclusive of that day, so at today's date of 12 October 2026 the window is plainly open; a transaction posted on 29 July would sit exactly on the final day today and would still be in time.

temporal_feasibility.condition: The benefit period the load belonged to ended no later than the expiry day counted from the last day of that benefit period.

temporal_basis.anchor_event: the last day of that benefit period
temporal_basis.counting_rule: Calendar days are counted from the day after the last day of the benefit period, every day of the week counts, an allowance spent on the final day still counts as spent, and full 24-hour periods are never used in place of calendar days.

boundary_check.just_before: The third-quarter allowance, loaded on 1 July, reaches the end of its life only on 31 December 2026; counting the plan's five expiry days from the day after that gives 5 January 2027, so nothing may be taken back from it today and an entry against that load would be wrong.
boundary_check.at_boundary: The second-quarter allowance reached the end of its life on 30 September 2026; counting the plan's five expiry days from the day after that gives 5 October 2026, and the day is inclusive, so from 5 October onwards the entry may be booked. Today, 12 October 2026, is not before that day.

seed_consistency.check: The programme is on the Plus card, opened alongside a medical plan enrollment that stands active, and it starts on that enrollment's coverage effective date of 2026-02-01 rather than before it; the tier needs neither a Medicaid standing nor a chronic condition, and the member's profile carries neither. The card was posted on 2026-02-03, inside the ten first-card delivery days the tier gives, and activated on 2026-02-11, well inside the tier's 120-day activation window. The balance the record shows, 33.75, is the one deliberate exception to the ledger identity: it was last worked out before the two transactions the network refused were released, and the card's own entries come to 93.75.

A scheduled load of the tier's quarterly allowance, made available on the first day of its benefit period as the tier's quarterly load frequency and load day require; the first one, made on the day the programme opened, is cut to the whole months of the opening quarter that were left, which is why it reads 90.00 rather than 135.00, and carries the proration reason for that. No load falls after the programme end date, the programme being open.

A card transaction at a retailer whose spending category the tier makes the card good for, no larger than the tier's 250.00 per-transaction maximum and inside the per-day count; it carries an authorisation code where the network answered and none where it did not, and its settlement standing says whether it took money off the card. Its benefit period is the quarter its posting date falls in.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the one member profile matching the name and telephone number the caller gives, and read back her member reference number, Medicare identifier, date of birth and contact details.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Without the member reference number nothing else on the account can be looked up, and the profile carries the identifiers checked at verification.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Establish that the caller is the member whose card is about to be discussed and closed, by checking the date of birth and Medicare identifier she states against the profile.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: No balance may be read out and no entry written on the card until identity is established; the closing write disposes of the member's own money.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the member's allowance programme: its tier, its standing, the health plan carrying it, the benefit year, the day the programme started and the balance the card record shows.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The tier fixes every per-tier figure the four computations use, and the balance the record shows is the figure the standing-balance rule falls back on.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read every entry on the card: the four quarterly loads, the correcting load posted into the second quarter, each purchase with its retailer, category, channel and settlement standing, and the retailer's refund posted in June.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: These rows are what the money still standing on the card, the unspent allowance of the closed benefit period, the dental spending and the transaction still only authorised are all reconciled from; the refused and unsettled entries decide which counting rule applies.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the service requests standing on the account: the closure request waiting for the member's signature, and the purchase dispute recorded against the dental transaction of 2 October.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The closure request is the authority the closing write rests on and its status decides which day the balance is settled to; the dispute intake is where the enquiry into the dental charge sits.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the catalogue orders on the programme: the order placed this morning with its value, delivery service and standing, and the order delivered in July.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: An order still standing to be sent is what the closing balance waits on; its value and delivery service decide how much goes back, and the delivered July order is what the ceiling on that refund is measured against.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the member's optional supplemental benefit rider, its official name, its standing and the day its benefits became payable.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Whether a dental, vision and hearing rider is in force is the first condition of the rule deciding what another payer has met of the costs the card has already paid.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the rider's claim lines: the October line with its recognised amount and what the rider paid, the June line it settled earlier, and the March line it denied.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: What the rider paid and the amount the claims were recognised at are the two cross-product figures the money going back on the card is worked out from; the June and March lines fall outside the stretch looked at and are excluded.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the medical plan enrollment that carries the allowance: its tier, its standing and whether any last day of cover is recorded against it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The medical plan tier's own yearly dental allowance is the fall-back the other-payer rule uses where no rider is in force, and whether the enrollment is still in force bears on the card continuing at all.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the hidden desk action that books a credit against a named card transaction.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock and call pair; it changes nothing in the records and happens once for this action.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Put back on the card the part of the dental charge of 2 October that the member's rider has since met, as a credit entry naming that transaction and placed in the benefit period it belonged to.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The recovery credit policy is the only rule that produces this figure; until the credit stands on the card the money still standing on it, and so the balance given up at closing, is short by it.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.allowance_program_id: The reference number of the member's allowance programme, read from the programme lookup at action 2. Basis: the tool's own schema requires 'the reference number of the allowance programme whose card is credited, as it is returned by a lookup of the member's allowance programmes'. Uniqueness: exactly one allowance programme stands for this member in the benefit year 2026, so no other reference number can be meant.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: The member reference number, read from the member profile at action 0. Basis: the tool's schema requires 'the member reference number the programme belongs to, as it is returned by the member profile lookup'. Uniqueness: the profile lookup returned exactly one profile for the name and telephone number the caller gave, and every record on the call hangs off it.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_ledger_entry_id: The reference number of the settled dental transaction of 2 October on the card, read from the card entries at action 3. Basis: the tool's schema requires 'the reference number of the single card transaction this credit relates to'; the policy puts the money back against the transaction that carried the cost. Uniqueness: within the stretch the rule looks at it is the only settled transaction at a dental, vision or hearing provider, and it is the entry the member's standing dispute names; the refused transaction of the same day carries no money, and the dental transaction of 8 May falls outside the stretch.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.credit_amount: 47.00. The card gives the member seventy-five days to question a purchase and has been used at a dental, vision or hearing provider, so the stretch looked at runs back three whole months, which reaches the two transactions of 2 October and excludes the one of 8 May. Within that stretch the card carries a transaction at such a provider that the network refused, so what the card was charged counts the settled transactions alone: 95.00, not the 137.00 posted. The rider is in force and its own record shows it paid 192.00 on the claim it settled on 8 October, so that is what another payer has met; the claims recognised in the stretch come to 240.00, so what the member was left to bear is 240.00 less 192.00, which is 48.00. The card is one on which dental, vision and hearing costs may be met and has been used at such a provider, so the money going back is 95.00 less 48.00, which is 47.00, and it is not above the 95.00 the card was charged. The rider's June line, paid but settled outside the stretch, and its denied March line are both excluded by the rule's own window and status.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.benefit_period: 2026-Q4. Basis: the policy states that the money put back 'is placed in the benefit period the transaction it relates to belonged to, so that money coming back near the end of a period does not quietly become a fresh allowance', and the card entry for the 2 October transaction carries the benefit period 2026-Q4. Uniqueness: the label is copied from the transaction the credit names, so no other is available; 2026-Q2 belongs to a different load and a different dental transaction.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the hidden desk action that takes an unspent allowance back off the card at the close of its benefit period.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock and call pair; it changes nothing in the records and happens once for this action.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Take back off the card what was left unspent of the second-quarter allowance now that it has reached the end of its life, naming the load of 1 April it comes from.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The period-end expiry policy is the only rule that produces this figure; until it stands on the card, what has already been taken off the card is nil and the balance given up at closing is overstated by it.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.allowance_program_id: The reference number of the member's allowance programme, read from the programme lookup at action 2. Uniqueness: the profile lookup returned exactly one profile for the name and telephone number the caller gave, and every record on the call hangs off it.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_ledger_entry_id: The reference number of the quarterly load of 1 April carrying benefit period 2026-Q2, read from the card entries at action 3. Basis: the tool's schema requires 'the reference number of the single load entry whose unspent part is being taken back'. Uniqueness: the period whose allowance has reached the end of its life is 2026-Q2, and that period carries one scheduled load, of 1 April; the correcting load posted into the same period on 12 May names that scheduled load rather than standing on its own, and the first, third and fourth quarter loads carry other periods.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.expiry_amount: 53.65. Nine whole months of the benefit year have gone by on a tier loaded by calendar quarters, so the current period is the fourth; the card lets an unspent allowance carry into the next period, is loaded on calendar quarters and has taken four loads, so an allowance stands to the last day of the period after the one it was loaded for, which makes the period now ending 2026-Q2. More than one load was posted for that period — the scheduled 135.00 of 1 April and the correcting 10.00 of 12 May — so the allowance loaded for it is 145.00. The period carries a transaction the network refused, so what was spent in it counts the settled transactions alone, 50.15, and not the refused 18.00. The period carries a retailer's own refund of 12.45, so that is counted back in. What is unspent is 145.00 and 12.45 less 50.15, which is 107.30. The member spent 50.15, less than half of the 145.00 loaded, so the share that carries forward is measured on what is unspent; the card carries an allowance forward up to half of a period's allowance and an allowance was loaded for the period, so the share is a half and 53.65 carries forward. What is taken back is 107.30 less 53.65, which is 53.65.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.benefit_period: 2026-Q2. Basis: the policy takes back the allowance of 'the period that ended one whole period before the current one', which on this card is 2026-Q2, and the load being taken back carries that very label. Uniqueness: the entry must be placed in the period whose allowance it ends, and only one benefit period satisfies that on this card today.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the hidden desk action that stops a standing catalogue order and returns what it took off the card.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock and call pair; it changes nothing in the records and happens once for this action.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Stop the catalogue order placed this morning at the member's word and put back on the card the value of the items together with the expedited delivery charge it carried.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The standing-order refund policy is the only rule that produces this figure; while the order stands to be sent the closing balance cannot be fixed, and the money it took off the card is missing from it.

Uniqueness: it is the only order on the programme still standing to be sent; the July order stands delivered and cannot be stopped.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.refund_amount: 56.45. The order stands on the card and its own record shows the items came to 46.50, so that is the value of the items. It was sent by the expedited service on a tier that offers catalogue ordering, so the delivery charge it carried is the tier's expedited charge of 9.95. The member asks for it to be stopped on the day it was placed and it has not been despatched, so the value of the items and the delivery charge both come back, which is 56.45. The catalogue has taken more than one transaction from this card — 33.20 in July and 56.45 this morning — so the ceiling on what may go back is the largest of them, 56.45, and the figure is not above it.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.benefit_period: 2026-Q4. Basis: the policy states that 'the money returns to the benefit period the order was paid from rather than becoming a fresh allowance', and the catalogue transaction of 12 October on the card carries the benefit period 2026-Q4. Uniqueness: the label is copied from the transaction the order was paid by, so no other is available; the July catalogue transaction belongs to a different order and to 2026-Q3.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.cancellation_reason: member_request. Basis: the tool's schema gives the closed set and states that member_request applies 'where the member themselves asks for the order to be stopped'; the member, told the order has not gone out, says to stop it and put the money back on the card. Uniqueness: item_out_of_stock does not hold because the plan can supply the items; insufficient_allowance does not hold because the card stands well above the order's value; address_undeliverable does not hold because no carrier has failed to deliver; programme_closed does not hold because the programme is still open at the moment the order is stopped; not_applicable is for an order that stands and is not being cancelled at all.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the member's own action for closing her allowance programme and hand it to her.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Giving up the card and the money on it is the member's own act; the desk arranges it and the member performs it.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Close the allowance programme on the member's own instruction, recording the last day the allowance could be spent and giving up the balance still standing on the card in one closing entry.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The closing balance policy is the only rule that produces this figure, and the closure itself may only be made by the member; it is the act the whole call was about.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.allowance_program_id: The reference number of the member's allowance programme, which the representative reads out to her from the programme record obtained at action 2. Basis: the tool's schema requires 'the reference number of the allowance programme being closed, which the representative reads out from the member's allowance programme record'. Uniqueness: one programme stands for this member in the benefit year.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.allowance_benefit_request_id: The reference number of the closure request standing on the account, which the representative reads out to her from the service requests obtained at action 4. Basis: the tool's schema requires 'the reference number of the service request the member raised asking for the programme to be closed'. Uniqueness: exactly one service request on this account asks for the programme to be closed; the other asks for a purchase to be looked into.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.forfeited_balance: 118.90. The card carries transactions the network refused and one still only authorised, so what is still standing is worked out entry by entry: loads of 505.00, being the four quarterly loads and the correcting load of 12 May, and money put back of 115.90, being the retailer's refund of 12.45, the recovery credit of 47.00 and the stopped order's 56.45, less the 423.70 of transactions that settled and less the 53.65 already taken off for the second quarter, which leaves 143.55. The card record's own figure of 83.55 is not used because refused and unsettled transactions stand on the card. The card record carries no last day on which the allowance could be spent and the closure request is waiting for the member's signature, so the balance is settled as it stands on the day she gives that signature. One transaction stands authorised and not settled, of 24.65 made on 9 October, three days before the closing day, which is no longer before it than the five days the tier allows a retailer to send a refund in, so the whole 24.65 is kept back. The balance given up is 143.55 less 24.65, which is 118.90.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.program_end_date: 2026-10-12. Basis: the tool's schema requires 'the last day the allowance could be spent, written as YYYY-MM-DD'; the policy fixes the closing day as 'the day the member gives their signature to the request' where the card record carries no last day of spending and the request waits for that signature, and that day is the day of this call. Uniqueness: the record carries no other last day of spending, and the day the request was taken, 5 October, applies only where the request is not waiting for a signature.

edges.condition: Every card transaction at a dental, vision or hearing provider that the member's other cover has since paid its part of carries a credit entry against it on the card's running record.
edges.policy_source: The balance given up on the closing day is not fixed until every card transaction at a dental, vision or hearing provider that the member's other cover has since paid its part of carries on the card the money put back for it.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The settled dental transaction of 2 October is one the member's other cover has since paid its part of: the rider settled the same treatment on 8 October, paying 192.00 of the 240.00 recognised. No credit entry names that transaction on the card: the only money put back anywhere on the card is the retailer's refund of 20 June, which names a different purchase and carries the retailer's own reason.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Once the recovery credit is booked, a credit entry of 47.00 names that transaction on the card and the money put back counted into the balance still standing rises from 68.90 to 115.90, taking the balance given up from 71.90 to 118.90.

edges.condition: The allowance of the benefit period whose life has ended carries an entry on the card's running record taking back what was left unspent from it.
edges.policy_source: The balance given up on the closing day is worked out only after the allowance of the benefit period whose life has ended stands taken back on the card.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The allowance loaded for benefit period 2026-Q2, the scheduled load of 1 April together with the correcting load of 12 May, reached the end of its life on 30 September, the card carrying an allowance forward one further period, and the plan's five expiry days ran out on 5 October. No entry on the card takes anything back from it: the card's running record carries no entry at all of the kind that ends a benefit period's allowance.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Once the expiry is booked, an entry of 53.65 stands against that load and what has already been taken off the card rises from nothing to 53.65, taking the balance given up from 172.55 to 118.90.

edges.condition: No catalogue order stands against the card waiting to be sent.
edges.policy_source: The balance given up on the closing day is not worked out before the card shows no catalogue order left standing to be sent.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The catalogue order placed on 12 October stands at placed with no tracking reference against it, so it is still waiting to be sent, and the 56.45 it took off the card on the day it was placed has not come back. The other catalogue order on the programme stands delivered and is not waiting for anything.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Once the order is stopped, it stands cancelled, nothing is left waiting to be sent, and 56.45 is put back on the card, taking the balance given up from 62.45 to 118.90.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The three prerequisites are parallel: none is a prerequisite of another, and they may be written in any of the six orders. They were replayed in all six orders with the same closing write at the end, and the terminal database was byte-identical every time, because each touches a disjoint object and each tool's row identifiers are derived from its own arguments rather than from the order of the call: the recovery credit names the dental transaction of 2 October, the expiry names the second-quarter load, and the stopped order names the catalogue order placed this morning. None of the three reads a quantity another writes: the recovery credit reads only dental card spending and the rider's claims; the expiry reads only entries carrying the 2026-Q2 label, which none of the other two writes; and the stopped order reads only the catalogue orders and the transactions the catalogue took. The root reads all three and is therefore last on every order.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the recovery credit and replaying everything else leaves the scored closing balance at 71.90 instead of 118.90: the money put back counted into what is still standing falls by 47.00.

Skipping the expiry and replaying everything else leaves the scored closing balance at 172.55 instead of 118.90: what has already been taken off the card falls to nothing, so 53.65 that should have gone back to the plan is given up by the member instead.

Skipping the stopped order and replaying everything else leaves the scored closing balance at 62.45 instead of 118.90: the 56.45 the order took off the card never comes back, and the terminal state also keeps a catalogue order standing at placed on a closed programme.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona names none of the three prerequisite problems and nothing that would point at them. She asks only to have the card closed and to be told what happens to the money on it. She never mentions the dental charge, the rider's payment or any dispute unless the representative asks her about the dental work, and then she says only that she paid the practice with the card and that the rider people wrote to her afterwards, with no amounts. She never mentions a benefit period, an allowance running out or anything expiring. She never mentions the catalogue order: it reaches the conversation only if the representative tells her an order has not gone out and asks what she wants done, and her reply is a reaction to that. She offers no hint of the shape 'is there something to sort out first' and never presses the representative toward any of the three. The one figure she volunteers, 33.75, is the balance the automated line read her, which is the card record's own stale figure and points at no prerequisite.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: No task tool validates a prerequisite. close_allowance_programme_5a9eaadb creates the closing entry and updates the programme with whatever forfeited_balance it is given; it looks up the programme only to copy the member reference onto the entry, and it neither reads the catalogue orders, nor counts expiry entries, nor checks for credits, nor errors on any of them. Called first, with the prerequisites unresolved, it books a closing entry of whatever figure was passed and closes the programme; the loss shows up only as a different terminal hash. post_dispute_credit_634307a6, post_period_expiry_1d3932f1 and cancel_catalog_order_88277d51 likewise write faithfully whatever they are given: none reads another problem's rows, none refuses, none hints, and none returns a policy-based error.

factor_trace: recovery_lookback (method): rested on the tier's 75-day dispute window and on the three dental transactions standing on the card, which satisfied both parts of its second tier; the stretch looked at therefore runs back three whole months, reaching the two transactions of 2 October and leaving the one of 8 May outside. The baseline reads the whole of the benefit year to date, which would have drawn in the May transaction and the rider's June line and given 5.00.

recovery_charge_counted (method): rested on the refused dental transaction of 42.00 of 2 October, which put the card on the first tier, so what the card was charged counts the settled transactions alone, 95.00. The baseline counts every transaction posted at such providers in the stretch, 137.00, and would have given 89.00.

recovery_other_payer (parameter, cross-difficulty): rested on the rider record standing active and on its settled claim line of 8 October paying 192.00, which satisfied both parts of the first tier. The baseline is nothing, which would have left the member bearing the whole 240.00 and given 0.00.
